briefs.source_chain: MSFT/Meta guide above consensus -> GS raises 2026 capex to $751B from $671B; underlying driver is supply not demand: HBM/CoWoS sold out through 1H27 -> four largest buyers pull 2027 orders forward -> that supply lock is why the cycle extends rather than peaks; separately, rising HBM prices (+18% into 1Q27) keep pushing capex guides higher because the constraint is supply; therefore Buy NVDA $250 PT; invalidated if HBM contract prices fall two consecutive months -> pull-forward argument breaks -> 2027 guides get cut; a Fed rate decision is not expected to change this.
briefs.brief_chain: MSFT/Meta guide above consensus -> GS raises 2026 capex to $751B from $671B; mechanism is supply not appetite: four largest buyers pull 2027 orders forward to lock sold-out HBM/CoWoS capacity through 1H27; because the constraint is supply, rising HBM prices (+18% into 1Q27) push capex guides higher, so the cycle extends rather than peaks; Buy NVDA $250 PT; invalidation is HBM prices falling two months running, breaking the pull-forward argument and cutting 2027 guides; Fed decision not expected to change the picture.

distortions.what: Source treats the supply-lock pull-forward and the rising-memory-price effect as two distinct supporting mechanisms (the former is why the cycle extends, the latter separately reinforces rising capex guides). The brief compresses them into a single causal chain where rising prices are presented as the direct cause of the cycle extending.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — both framings converge on the same call (Buy NVDA, $250 PT) and the same invalidation condition (HBM prices falling two months running), so acting on the brief instead of the source produces an identical trade.
